title: Fleet Management
summary: One parking change used to mean an email, 37 folders and a 48-column spreadsheet. The app puts the three things behind it in one place: look up a plate, request a change, approve it.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Process design, data model, front end, back end

facts.label: Scope
facts.value: One record per plate · a floor plan per site · several changes per request

steps.label: Look up
steps.hint: DEMO 101 is loaded; try a site for its floor plan

steps.label: Request
steps.hint: pick a change type; the form pre-fills what it knows

sections.heading: The problem
paragraphs: A vehicle changes bay. Someone emails: maybe five vehicles, old bays, new bays, in whatever layout the sender likes. The receiver checks which floor the new bay is on and whether it is free — across 37 folders — then edits a 48-column Excel by hand. Three places, three chances to mistype a plate.

sections.heading: Look up
paragraphs: Type a plate and the whole record comes out, the bay drawn on its floor plan. Search by site instead and the plan shows every plate on its bay.

sections.heading: Request
paragraphs: Enter the plate, pick the change type, and the form pre-fills what it already knows. Existing values are suggested as you type, so one department is not spelled three ways. Several changes go in one submission.

sections.heading: Approve
paragraphs: The administrator approves or returns each request in the same place, grouped by plate, so a batch cannot be half-done. Approved rows can be copied into the logbook in the column order the existing macro expects.

sections.heading: What the public demo withholds
paragraphs: The employer is not named. The fleet is synthetic (DEMO 101–136, Parking Site 01–10); identity and financial fields render as explicit "Redacted" bars; the floor plans are schematic.
